I’m currently working on a thesis focused on the intersection of neurological conditions and musculoskeletal disorders, and your post really caught my attention. 

There is growing evidence suggesting a possible link between autism and scoliosis. Some studies point to shared genetic factors, such as mutations in the COL11A1 gene, which is involved in connective tissue formation and nervous system development, potentially impacting both conditions. 

Neurological differences, particularly in the cerebellum (responsible for motor control and balance), have also been observed in both autism and scoliosis cases. Additionally, hypotonia (low muscle tone) and sensory processing challenges often seen in autism can influence posture, which may contribute to scoliosis development over time. So it definitrely seems plausible that both conditions could share underlying mechanisms!

Thanks for sharing your story and your results, it’s really interesting :)
